speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you're experiencing wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; tell me, when did these symptoms first start?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Borrelia burgdorferi infection) presenting with early disseminated symptoms.

The combination of recent Minnesota camping, self-resolving monoarthritis, and now wrist pain with fever is highly suggestive of Lyme arthritis. I need to confirm the skin lesion details and check for neurological signs. REQUEST TEST: Erythema_Chromicum_Migrans_history. REQUEST TEST: Lyme_Serology (ELISA and Western Blot).
